summary: Submitted a feedback-only research product that closes the last open premise of this session, with preflight returning valid:true. The premise carried by two earlier products - that a non-voter might be elected, with the refusal mechanism unidentified - is now answered: repeating the leadership-transfer prefix with the library's own debug logging visible shows every voter logging that it rejects the vote request because the node is not a voter, so the campaigning non-voter never accumulates a quorum (its own vote is not counted either, since the self-vote branch is restricted to voters) and returns to follower while a voter wins its own election. The source states the guard and its purpose: a vote or pre-vote request from a server without a vote is answered with the term adopted and the vote refused, so that a node converted from voter to non-voter cannot block progress, with the upstream change referenced in the comment. The premise is therefore refuted by an intentional check rather than by race timing, and the 'contending voter election' explanation is no longer needed; no obligation is warranted. Remaining kept visible: the transfer path still accepts a non-voter as a target and in the exercised prefix reported success while the cluster had no leader until a voter re-elected itself, uncovered by any obligation and not stated as intended by any source read; the repair locations for the three newest obligations remain open; the deferred third-party-transport and nested-module surfaces remain unread, with the MonotonicLogStore status unchanged and its last-log anomaly closed last turn; and all non-voter prefixes plus this explanation were draft construction work, so no property evidence is claimed. ref_ids cite only existing objects (s-raft-request-vote-filter, s-raft-pre-vote, b-vote-grant, b-pre-vote-grant, f-leadership-held, s-raft-timeout-now) and no map change is claimed. Run state: ten confirmed in-scope findings across eight checked units, audit spec v13, 2 audit units, 21 experiments, 11 semantic reviews and roughly four minutes remaining.
